title: Fame Level: Low
text: “Alright, Queen, Ren, and… well, the rest doesn’t matter—let’s pass through the castle town and head to the castle.”
“Leave the gate to me, I say!”
“I want to cause some chaos too, so I won’t hold back on smashing through.”
“Ren, try to make it sound like a proper declaration, okay?”
“Shut up! You lot are all going to pay for this later!”
And so, we arrived at the castle town of Melromarc.
“Hm!? You are—!?”
The moment we tried to enter the castle town, a soldier standing guard on the main street noticed the queen and the others.
“For some reason I find myself back in the country, and now this uproar!? Hurry and let us through to the castle at once!”
At the queen’s declaration, the soldier blew a whistle and shouted in response.
“You cannot possibly be Her Majesty the Queen! Men! Deal with this insolent impostor immediately!”
“Ho… you’d say the same thing even with me standing right here?”
Ren declared, stepping forward as if to shield the queen.
“After I went to all the trouble of bringing her here, and you still call her an impostor?”
“Guh…”

At the sound of the whistle summoning reinforcements, soldiers and Three Heroes Church faithful came rushing over one after another. Naturally, behind them, the townsfolk gathered too, gawking like spectators at some show. Ren’s face was well known, after all. And yet the look on Ren’s expression seemed to be one of… anticipation, as if hoping someone would just go ahead and declare the queen a fraud already.
“Sword Hero-sama! Please, do not lend your ear to the words of these impostors posing as Her Majesty! Please, allow us to capture these frauds and bring them before you!”
“How insolent… so this is how far you’ve fallen. Aultcray, do you understand? This too is a debt we brought upon ourselves.”
The queen scolded Trash in a cold tone.
“Hmph. These men were originally proper Melromarc soldiers.”
Trash, too, showed no sign of backing down.
Incidentally, Ren’s lines were being whispered to him by Father.

“The line is: ‘The true queen, having returned to reclaim her castle now cast in shadow, shall restore it to its rightful form—a triumphant parade of illusion-breaking. Judgment shall be passed upon any who dare obstruct our righteous path—a moment of brave judgment. If you do not wish to be banished, then step aside!’ That’s the line, got it?”
“I— there’s no way I’m saying something like that!”
It seemed Father had tried to have him deliver it in Rafumi’s speech pattern, but Ren apparently translated it into ordinary speech instead.
“Ahem! Whether this is the genuine article shall be determined once we reach the castle. Now then—make way!”
“Even if you are the Sword Hero-sama, we cannot allow a false claimant into the castle! Everyone! Strike these impostors down!”
Ignoring Ren’s declaration, the soldiers each drew their weapons and lunged forward. Ren glanced briefly at me and Itsuki, then raised his sword high into the air and shouted.
“Foolish lot! Hundred Sword Ⅴ!”
With Ren’s skill, countless swords materialized in midair and rained down upon the soldiers.
“““Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!?”””

The soldiers were sent flying by the aftershock of the skill. Though it seemed he’d held back somewhat, as the soldiers lay sprawled on the ground, there didn’t appear to be many fatalities among them.
“Trying not to kill them, are we? How soft. These are men who defied the king’s command and made the country their own plaything—immediate execution would surely suffice, wouldn’t it?”
Itsuki asked, wearing an unpleasant smile as he turned to the queen and Trash, silently seeking permission to finish the job.
“…Allow me to handle the binding magic here. Icicle Prison!”
Crack! The queen encased the fallen soldiers in ice, rendering them immobile.
“Good grief… I do think the rot in this nation ought to be dealt with swiftly. Well, if this pitiful number is all they could muster, I suppose there’s nothing to be done about it.”

“Haah… Itsuki, don’t make that face like you’re disappointed more soldiers didn’t show up so you could cut loose. The townspeople… well, I guess it’s fine since they’re just watching from a distance.”
“S-someone! Don’t let them into the castle town! A reward to whoever stops them!”

What appeared to be the captain of the guard cried out for help toward the townsfolk. A pathetic sight. The town’s residents could only watch from a distance, gulping nervously. Well, considering that anyone who dared to attack would likely be cut down on the spot, that was understandable. The national mood had been one of war fever—kill every demi-human and beastman, kill anyone associated with Father, the Shield Hero—but that fire had always been burning on the other side of the river, so to speak. And now, faced with the sight of the Sword Hero leading the queen and Trash back in triumphant return right before their very eyes, they clearly had no idea how to react. If Father, the Shield Hero, had been the one leading the charge, some might have attacked out of pure emotion—but with Ren as the representative, it seemed to be having quite the deterrent effect.
“Silence. You will receive a fitting punishment later.”
The queen encased the shouting soldier in even more ice to silence him and continued forward. Just then, a blowdart suddenly came flying, but Itsuki intercepted it.
“Even assassination darts, now? My, aren’t you thorough.”
“What in the world…”
Even Trash seemed at a loss for words at the shameless assassination attempt from the nation’s underbelly.
“Now then… let us proceed to the castle. You lot… out of the way.”
When Ren fixed the gawking townsfolk with a sharp glare, the crowd split neatly in two, opening a path to the castle. We continued onward, as if in a triumphant procession.
“Is that really the queen?”
“Bringing along demi-humans and beastmen, no less…”
“She was always in favor of peace with those Siltvelt folk, after all…”
“How dreadful… perhaps we really should have her step down and install someone new.”
The townsfolk murmured amongst themselves in hushed tones. Do you people even realize your nation’s situation isn’t stable enough for you to be running your mouths like that?
“It’s like this because Naofumi wasn’t able to be active within the country, nano. Things haven’t gone in a good direction, nano. Fame is important, nano.”

Rival muttered at the crowd, brow furrowed. She had a point. But that was simply the tradeoff—the result of choosing not to keep repeating the same tired approach. Just then, Itsuki shot an arrow at the hand of a child who’d been about to throw a stone in retaliation.
“Consider this a warning. Understand the weight of what it means to throw that stone…”
“Ugh… guh… what queen!? Taking the side of demi-humans and beastmen! Why would the Sword Hero-sama—”
“Bwoink!”
A pig held the child back, stopping them from stepping forward. A parent, perhaps?

“That’s because you people are the ones in the wrong. Torturing innocent demi-humans and beastmen for your own twisted satisfaction, indulging some hollow sense of righteousness at the expense of others’ suffering. You’ve learned something today, haven’t you?”
Itsuki lectured on.
“Itsuki, that… definitely isn’t getting through to that kid, you know?”
“Probably not. I know it isn’t the child’s fault either. I just… couldn’t help myself, seeing what looked like my past self standing there.”
“…Sooner or later, it will be made clear who was in the right. So… swallow whatever you’re thinking for now. Do not commit the grave sin of defying this nation’s king right here, right now.”

Ren stepped in to caution them and pressed forward, leading the way. It seemed Ren was well aware that he currently held the most authority to speak in this situation, occasionally pressing a hand to his mouth as if suppressing nausea. According to Father, he was apparently on the verge of throwing up from the stress. The burden of being treated as the foremost hero was weighing heavily on Ren. Well, Ren did have an unusually strong sense of responsibility. Precisely because he understood that someone had to do this in the current situation, he was barely enduring the pressure—or so it seemed. Meanwhile, he kept muttering under his breath, over and over: “Unforgivable, Rafumi. Because of you, all this is happening…” Mutter, mutter—quite the noisy one, wasn’t he.
